**I** IVI 

## **Longship**
Longships remain the favoured watercraft of the Norse Dwarfs, their shallow draft helping to navigate the rivers of Norsca as well as its coast. Though their initial design was not unlike the ships of their Norscan neighbours, new Longships integrate technology traded with the World’s Edge Dwarfs, replacing its Bolt Thrower with a Breaker Cannon, reinforcing gunwhales with steel, and installing a ‘grubark’ gearing system that allows a small group of Dwarfs to power whole banks of oars by themselves. 

Dwarf Longships increase their Move to 6 when at least 8 crew are working the oars. 

## **Gunboat**
Vital to their trade with Karaz-a-Karak and the rest of Karaz Ankor beyond it, the Dwarfs of Barak Varr fought hard to secure the route for its trade barges. Under threat from greenskins and Trolls, as well as less-thanneighbourly petty rulers among the Border Princes, the Dwarfkings found themselves forced to devote large numbers of warriors to protect the barges, both coming and going. Even then, losses could be heavy. 

Tasked by the Dwarfking to ‘do something’, in the 19th century IC the Engineers of Barak Varr came up with the ‘Gunboat’. An armour-clad, steam-driven ship the size of an Imperial patrol boat, about 25 feet long, the gunboat mounts its engine amidships for greater efficiency as it drives twin paddlewheels, one on each side. Gunboats usually carry a crew of eight — a captain, a pilot and his relief, four gunners, and an engineer to maintain the engine — but can carry up to a half-dozen more Dwarfs, if the threats warrant it. Regardless of crew numbers, all Dwarfs on a gunboat are trained warriors, ready to fight in addition to their other duties. To provide shelter at night, Barak Varr maintains a variety of fortified inn, the walls of which also provide protection to docked rivercraft, about a day’s travel from each other. Surrounded by often-hostile country, visitors other than Dwarfs are a rare sight. 

On escort duty or patrol, gunboats frequently travel in pairs for mutual support. Protecting a convoy, one will lead a group of barges, while the other brings up the rear, both on constant watch for ambushes. If on patrol and the need arises to check something onshore, one boat will stay on watch, while the crew of the other investigates. Barak Varr often sends small patrols such as these up the tributaries of the Skull and Blood rivers to make sure no threats are building in the ‘backcountry’. 

Gunboats mount a ram on the prow, which provides 5 Armour Points, and can be used to effectively neutralise boats of similar size by smashing into them. All other parts of the Gunboat have 2 Armour Points of protection. 

Each Gunboat mounts two turrets, which can be a Swivel Gun or Volley Gun. The forward gun rests in a ‘gun pit’ with a 180 degree firing arc, which provides hard cover to the crew (a –30 hit modifier on ranged attacks). The rear gun is on a raised platform with a 360 firing arc, providing medium cover (a –20 modifier on ranged attacks). 

## **Steam Barge**
Prior to the steam engine, barges travelling between Karaz Ankor and the Karaz-a-Karak road had to be towed upstream by mule teams, or even by gangs of Dawi pulling on tow ropes. This made the trips even more dangerous and costly, as the craft and their crews were vulnerable to attack. In times of turmoil, losses could be high, and the risk was always present that Barak Varr could be cut off from Karaz Ankor. 

Along with the gunboat, then, the hold’s Engineers developed a steam-powered barge that allowed each barge to be manned by fewer crew and travel in the middle of the river, farther from dangerous shores. Propelled by a single paddlewheel at the rear, the steam barge is a flat platform 30 feet in length and 10 feet wide, with low walls around the deck. The deck supports two small cabins, one at the rear for the engine and paddlewheel mechanism, the other in the middle for the crew. The usual crew consists of a captain, the Engineer, and two labourer Dwarfs. A reversed tiller at the bow controls two rudders used for steering. 

Other than the cabins, the deck is open for the carrying of cargo. When not powering the wheel, the steam engine is used to operate a collapsible crane for loading and unloading cargo in nets. With careful loading, the capacity of a steam barge is much greater than that of a large Imperial river barge, 800 Enc. 

Unarmoured, slow, and with only personal weapons for the crew, the steam barge is not made for combat. Instead, travelling in convoys of up to five barges, it relies on the protection of the escorting gunboats during the day and the fortified inns at night. 

**I** IVI 

## **Monitor**
Monitors were the firsts ships designed at Barak Varr, and were a response to the threat of pirates and other raiders to coastal shipping. They operate in and just beyond the Blood River delta and guard the approaches to Barak Varr, as well as the coasts as far west as the River Treblecz and the allied manling port of Somjek, and as far south as a day’s sailing from the hold. 

The steel hull sits low in the water, supporting a squat, enclosed top castle affectionately referred to as the ‘turtle’. From this arises both the funnel for the steam engine, which powers a single rear paddlewheel, and a gunnery turret that can rotate through a 270 degrees arc, its only ‘blind spot’ being where the funnel sits behind it. 

Crewed by 20-25 Dwarfs, Monitors are capable of attacking at range and by ramming. The turret mounts two cannon, usually Breakers, but some are field testing switching one for a flame cannon for use against wooden ships. Beyond the turret guns, Monitors are armed with up to five Breaker cannons on each side, for a formidable broadside. 

Their low freeboard limits their seaworthiness, however, as rough weather can swamp them. Monitors thus mainly serve a coastal defence role. To project power further out to sea, Barak Varr developed the Ironclad. Monitors are fitted with a ram, a turret, and 2 Armour Points of protection (as Gunboats). The turret usually mounts two Breaker Cannons, but replacing one with a Flame Cannon is a popular choice for use against wooden ships. Beyond the turret guns, Monitors are armed with up to five Breaker cannons on each side, for a formidable broadside. 

## **Ironclad**
Larger, more stable, and more heavily armed and armoured than a Monitor, the Ironclad is the mainstay of Barak Varr’s fleet, able to project power far out to sea or other lands. 

Dual paddlewheels, one on each side and each powered by its own engine, provide the Ironclad with after turns and much more manoeuvrability overall than not only a Monitor, but the ships of other species and nations. Crewed by 75 to 100 Dwarfs, Ironclads have two enclosed turrets, fore and aft. Each mount a battery of two Tempest cannons, while above and behind each of these is a secondary battery of one Breaker, each. Casements on each side provide space for a further four Breakers, each. 

Ironclads also have many small gun ports on each side for use during boarding actions, when the covering hatches are dropped and crew-dwarfs can sweep the enemy decks with swivel guns, volley guns, or even crossbows. 

Ironclads have 2 Armour Points of protection to all locations, with enclosed turrets to the fore and aft. Each mounts a battery of two Tempest Cannons, with a Breaker Cannon above and behind each turret. Casements provide space for a further four Breaker Cannons on each side. Ironclads also have many small gun ports on each side for use during boarding actions, when the covering hatches are dropped and crew can sweep the enemy decks with swivel guns, volley guns, or crossbows. 

## **Dreadnought**
The Dreadnought is the latest evolution of Barak Varr’s surface ships, an immense warship capable of sinking an entire enemy flotilla on its own. With the farthest range of any Dwarf warship as well as awesome size and armament, the Kings of Barak Varr have often chosen the Dreadnought to ‘show the colours’ in other lands, whenever necessary to impress — or intimidate — outsiders. 

Three great paddlewheels, one on each side and a larger one at the stern, propel the Dreadnoughts the length of the Black Gulf and far out into the Southern Sea. A great engine room, more complex and powerful than any yet designed by Barak Varr’s naval workshops, powers the wheels and the ships turrets and steering system. More heavily armed than any previous class of Dwarf ship, there are two turrets each fore and aft, one in each pair mounted above and behind the other. Each turret mounts a pair of Thunder cannon — a salvo from these is so powerful, it would roll or tear apart any ship less massive than a Dreadnought. Two smaller turrets higher up toward the bridge each support a single Tempest cannon, while five Breaker cannons on each side add to a broadside. Rounding out its armaments, like Ironclads, the Dreadnought has small ports used for anti-personnel fire against enemy ships. 

Dreadnoughts have 2 Armour Points of protection to all locations. At the fore and aft, two turrets bear two Thunder Cannons each, for eight Thunder Cannons in total. Each pair of turrets is positioned so that one is above and behind the other. Towards the bridge, two higher, smaller turrets bear a Tempest Cannon each, and five Breaker Cannons on each side provide a broadside. Like Ironclads, Dreadnoughts have small ports used for anti-personnel fire against enemy ships. 

**I** IVI 

Alternate weapon configurations are common, to suit the preferences of the Engineer who crafted it, and the Admiral in command. For example, _Grudgebreaker_ -class battleships mount only one turret of three Thunder Cannons, to make space for the launch pad of a small combat dirigible. 

## **Nautilus Submersible**
The oddest class of ship in Barak Varr’s fleet, the Nautilus steam submersible is capable of travelling both on and below the surface of the water. When on the surface, it resembles nothing so much as a Monitor, but with two turrets, one fore and aft, each housing a single Breaker cannon. Instead of a ram, two torpedo tubes are mounted in the bow. The only ship not to use paddlewheels, submersibles move by means of dual screws. 

The Nautilus’s most notable feature is its ability to submerge under the waves, travel underwater, and stay there for extended periods of time. When the captain gives the order, the crew seals the hatches tight, opens a set of valves and floods the ballast tanks in the hull. With a trained crew, a submersible can vanish beneath the waves in less than a minute. To surface, air from compressed tanks is forced into the ballast tanks, pushing the water out. 

Nautilus Submersibles are armed with two Breaker Cannon turrets (fore and aft), with two Nautilus Torpedoes ready to fire from a pair of tubes mounted in the bow. 

The Nautilus can safely dive to a depth of 30 yards, and stay there for up to one hour. Whilst underwater, it reduces its Move to 2, and cannot fire its Breaker Cannons. However, it may still fire its Nautilus Torpedoes, and is effectively immune to enemy fire — unless the enemy has a means to launch underwater attacks, or can force the submersible to resurface. 

After one hour, the effects of oxygen depletion and boiler fumes begin to suffocate the Nautilus’ crew ( **WFRP Core Rulebook** ), unless the vessel resurfaces for at least three hours. Consequently, Nautilus captains prefer to travel on the surface, diving only when absolutely necessary. 

A Nautilus Submersible can push itself to greater depths of 30 yards, but doing so places extraordinary pressure upon the vessel’s hull. The Nautilus makes a **Challenging (+0) Toughness** Test every 10 minutes or so it spends at lower depths, with increased difficulties for extreme depths. If the Test is failed, the vehicle suffers 30 Wounds from springing leaks and the buckling hull. A trained crew can make Sail (Nautilus) and Trade (Engineer) Tests to anticipate the submersible’s limits, safely resurfacing before Toughness Tests become necessary. 

Submersibles normally have a crew complement of 20, but finding sufficient crew can sometimes be difficult. While the Dwarfs of Barak Varr can overcome the traditional Dawi aversion to not being on or under land, the idea of going under the water is too much for most. The assumption is that a Dwarf must be somewhat unhinged to actually want to do this. 

But there are Dwarfs daring and even reckless enough to do this. Joining a Nautilus crew, where casualties can be high, is for some an alternative to expiating shame by taking the Slayer’s oath. Indeed, the King of Barak Varr has formally offered the choice of submersible service, instead of becoming a Slayer, a proposition that has been learned of and taken up by others of distant holds. 

## Slaughter at Blood River
Raiders from the Badlands have attacked convoys of steam barges along the Skull River in larger numbers than usual, disrupting vital trade. The king of Barak Varr, Zamnil Grundisson, wants to know why, so he can put a stop to it. The Characters are a group of Dawi and perhaps Dawikoni he assigns to investigate. Travelling at night in a gunboat specially modified for quieter running, the Characters are taken far up the Blood River, where it is suspected the raiders have their camp. The gunboat will wait up to a week for the Characters to return, then assume they have met a bitter fate and leave. 

The Characters find the outlaws’ camp after a couple of days, but make a starting discovery — the bandits have been wiped out. They find over 100 bodies hacked, torn, even partially eaten, and not that long ago. Any loot they stole is missing, too. What killed them, and does it pose a threat to Barak Varr? The King needs to know. 

**I** IVI 

## The Legend of Captain Nihmok
Rogue Engineers are not unknown in Karaz Ankor, but few are as colourful or infamous as Logazor Nihmok of Barak Varr, also known as ‘Captain Nihmok’. A brilliant Engineer fascinated by the sea in a way unusual even for the Dwarfs of Barak Varr, he specialised in submersibles. Quickly gaining a reputation as a bold experimenter — or a ‘reckless fool’, depending on perspective — Nihmok pushed the limits of his designs and his crews, putting them both at risk, and sometimes losing both tragically. 

But, he was not deterred. Barak Varr’s enemies at sea were many, and the hold needed every technological edge it could get. When he could not find a willing captain for his latest craft, Nihmok took the role himself and became as daring a commander as he was an Engineer. His underwater raid into Sartosa harbour, the heart of the pirate isle, became legendary in Karaz Ankor. 

Then came the split. Known to be critical of King Zamnil for being too cautious, Captain Nihmok sought a private audience with the King to propose a great raid against the enemy. Just which enemy and what was proposed is a mystery, however. They had met alone, and all that those outside the throne room could hear was a 

lot of muffled shouting that climaxed in the King and the Captain exchanging heated accusations. 

At that and without a further word, Captain Nihmok stalked out of the throne room, never to be seen in Barak Varr again. The next morning, harbour workers discovered his latest Nautilus, the _Hammer of the Sea_ was gone, as was its crew and Nihmok himself. After weeks of no word, rumour reached Barak Varr of a renegade Nautilus attacking ships from the Black Gulf to the coast of Bretonnia. It was the _Hammer_ . 

The pattern of his targets made no sense. He would strike Sartosan pirates, the ships of the Dark Elves, even Marienburg merchantmen. And yet, at least in the case of Human crews, he would rescue survivors and set them ashore, before vanishing back under the waves. And, just as strange, the reports said he refused to ever again set foot on land. 

No one knows why Captain Nihmok does this, nor where his secret base is and how he replenishes his supplies. But several nations have proclaimed large rewards for his capture or death. Strangely, King Zamnil is not one of them. 

## **Torpedo**
Unique to the submersibles of Barak Varr, the torpedo is a long, streamlined self-propelled projectile that can strike enemy vessels beneath their waterline. An intricate clockwork motor powers a four-bladed propeller, while the forward end carries a timed explosive powerful enough to cripple even a large vessel. Each submersible carries four, which may be fired either while on the surface or, ideally, from below at an unsuspecting enemy. 

## The Guns of Navak-Rhon
The Dwarf mines of Navak-Rhon, owned by Zhufbar and recently the site of a major gromril strike, have been captured by the Greenskins. The Dwarfking intends to send an army to recover it and settle the grudge, but the mines were strongly defended by heavy artillery. The Characters are an ‘assault team’ sent to infiltrate Navak-Rhon and spike the guns before the army arrives. Otherwise, it will be cut to ribbons.

## Runic Weapons of Renown
## **Barrakul**
Barrakul, translated as ‘Hope of the Mountains’, is a Runic Longsword crafted by an unknown Runesmith and historically wielded by the one-eyed Daemon Slayer Harbek Armgusson, and by the Human Templar Siegfried von Kesselring. 

A shining longsword, sheathed in a gem-encrusted leather scabbard with finely inlaid metalwork, the runes of the weapon glow ruby, etched down the blade. When drawn and used in combat, it is said that the blade flows through visibility, at first sight a sharp and clean blade, then an empty space the next, leaving only the floating red runes below the hilt, before reappearing the other side of its victim. The sword is also said to be able to bypass any non-magical protection, phasing through shields and armour alike. 

The weapon was originally taken from the corpse of an Orc whose Warband was found desecrating a temple to the Ancestor Gods, slain by Harbek and his band. Though an initial investigation into the blade provided no answers as to its origins, no extensive effort was made to further research the blade’s creation, for fear of being honour bound to return the weapon. 

The ultimate fate of the Slayer, whether he achieved his oath of dying in glorious combat, or lost his life in any number of potentially lethal adventuring exploits, is unknown. What is known is that after his passing, the sword was given into the possession of one of his travelling companions, a rare Dwarven Priest of the Cult of Sigmar. It is believed that the weapon was then passed down, through the cult, until it was wielded by Siegfried von Kesselring. 

Siegfried, a Templar and loyal servant of Sigmar, was visiting a newly constructed temple in Wittgendorf when the town came under attack by a Beastman horde, led by a Warrior of Chaos. After seeing to the evacuation of the citizens and leading what defence he could, he was forced to fall back to the temple, where he swore an oath to allow not one enemy inside. 

Von Kesselring is said to have fought on the steps for a number of hours. Filled with a righteous fury and with an uplifting zeal, he slew countless foes, including the Chaos Marauder, and was able to maintain his defence until reinforcements from a nearby town arrived to help, but he would ultimately succumb to his wounds. He was honoured and interred within the temple’s crypt bearing Barrakul, in a funeral conducted by the Grand Theogonist himself. Many hundreds of years later, the crypt would be investigated and Von Kesselring’s tomb opened. His body had decayed to bones and his armour rusted away, but Barrakul sat pristine and sparkling upon his corpse. 

## **Bryngandaz**
Bryngandaz is a rune-etched Pick, whose name can be translated from Khazalid as ‘Goldfinder’. The instrument, both tool and weapon, was crafted for the Miner Kings of Ekrund during the Golden Age of Karaz Ankor. The first records of its use in combat come from when Ekrund joined forces with Karak Azgul and Barak Varr to put the torch to the Elf Colonies of Tilea. Miner King Ekkel Olivsson was at the forefront of the battles, with Goldfinder in hand. 

It was in -1498 IC that the great wealth of Ekrund caught the eye of the Greenskin warhosts and enticed them to the Dragonback Mountains, where the Miner King Murkan Ekkelsson was tasked with defending his realm and driving them back. Though he put on a valiant defence of the Dwarf hold and wielded Bryngandaz with ruthless effect, he would ultimately be outnumbered and surrounded. Taking direct command of a unit of elite Longbeards, the Miner King led a desperate charge that broke through the encirclement and held it open long enough for the Clans to flee through to the shores of the Black Gulf, where their allies Barak Varr had sent ships to evacuate them. 

Seeing the need to hold back the crush of enemies from those fleeing, Murkan and his forces chose to fight their way back into the Dwarf hold, to make a last stand in their ancestral home. Though they carved a bloody swathe through the enemy, eventually Miner King Murkan realised that their expected doom drew near. He chose to protect Bryngandaz from Orc hands, and sealed the weapon in a hidden chamber deep in Ekrund, before taking a runesword from a fallen comrade and continuing in his final stand. He and his fellows took a large number of Orcs with them and would ultimately fall, but succeeded in their goal of drawing the attention of their enemies long enough for the evacuation to complete. 

**I** IVI 

There are many who believe that the famed pick would not have been allowed to fall into enemy hands, and that it must therefore remain hidden in the depths of Ekrund, almost certainly surrounded by various traps, waiting to be found. Others claim that, given the sheer number of Goblin and Orc clans that have roamed through the mine, it must certainly have fallen into their hands and if it did, where could it have gone? Could it have remained in Orc held territory in the nearby World’s Edge Mountains? Or taken out into the Badlands? Miner Kings in exile have long sought any information or rumour that could hint at the current location of the legendary pick. 

## **Ghal Maraz**
Ghal Maraz, known as the ‘Hammer of Sigmar’ to Humans or ‘Skull-Splitter’ in the Dwarfen tongue, is the magical warhammer famously brandished by Sigmar Heldenhammer himself. 

Creation of the hammer is attributed to the venerated Ancestor God Smednir, at the dawn of time. Even the most masterfully crafted weapon cannot contain the power of more than three runes, but such is the power of Ghal Maraz that, depending on what source you listen to, it is believed to house as many as five. 

While the Cult of Sigmar and the Imperial government both state that the hammer wielded by Karl Franz is the original hammer given to Sigmar in his time before his ascension, it is argued that the powers that the hammer should grant its user appear not to match those told in tales of old, though dismissed as a simple fact of fanciful retellings according to Imperial Scholars. 

The truth of the matter is that the hammer handed down through the succession of Emperors was in fact a masterfully crafted duplicate, blessed by Sigmarite Priests and crafted by expert Runesmiths, granting those that held it increased strength, renewing their vitality and allowing their attacks to bypass non-magical armour. 

Following an encounter between adventurers and the Tzeentchian Lord of Change Sheerargetru in the Black Fire Pass during the civil strife of the Turmoil of 2512 IC, the true Ghal Maraz was discovered and quickly returned to Karl Franz, who has wielded it ever since. 

Very few knew of the replacement, as not only were the abilities of Ghal Maraz considered a state secret within the Empire, the creation of the replacement was another great secret tightly held by Karaz Ankor, who did not inform their Human allies of the exchange. 

Gifted to Prince Sigmar as thanks when he and his Unberogen warriors assisted in the rescue of the Dwarf High King Kurgan Ironbeard from the Orc Warlord Vagraz Headstomper and his force of Greenskins, and as a symbol of the friendship long shared between Dwarf and the Unberogen tribe of Men. When Sigmar felt his years coming to a close, he abdicated his throne and endeavoured to return the hammer to the High King of Karaz Ankor that had gifted it to him, only for he and the hammer to disappear when he entered the Black Fire Pass. 

In 500 I.C, an Imperial Dwarf delegation would return the hammer to Emperor Sigismund II. To hear them tell it, a human had brought the hammer to Karaz-a-Karak a few years after Sigmar disappeared, presenting it to the High King and leaving without giving his name. They claimed that the hammer remained among the heirlooms of the clan, until the High King was visited by Grungni in a dream where he bade him return the hammer to the humans, as a time was coming when they would need it. 

Most notably, it is of contested historical record whether this hammer wielded by Emperor Sigismund II and the subsequent Emperors up until Karl Franz is the Ghal Maraz of legend. This is referred to as the “Two Hammer Theory” by those that would find themselves on the gibbet not long after. 

**I** IVI 

## **Gnoldron**
A Runic Hammer created by the Runesmith Arnek Ragasson during the War of Vengeance, translated from Khazalid as ‘Old Thunder’. Reputed to be the favoured hammer of the Funimrik clan of the Karak Vlag Runesmith craft guild, the weapon gained fame through numerous conflicts, attributed with the destruction of the gates of many Elf strongholds and with taking the heads of numerous war bosses in skirmishes against the Greenskin foe. The greatest tale told of the warhammer would be its use in the slaying of the dragon Ioridrak by the Runesmith Chrobak Ironarm, who is said to have spent weeks carefully crafted his own specialised equipment, carving into it a number of runes aimed specifically at his quarry. He made and used a cloak brooch with the Rune of the Furnace, a ring with the Rune of Healing should the battle be drawn out and boots with the Rune of Lightfoot, should the large size of his adversary cause his footing to be lost. 

The hammer itself is said to be capable of throwing bolts of lightning at distant targets, and emitting a crack of thunder with each hit it delivers. There are also old mentions of the weapon granting the wielder protection from similar forms of magic. No known Master Rune that exists today is capable of these feats, implying that the one engraved into Gnoldron has been lost to time. For obvious reasons, information on the weapon is frequently sought by those versed in the research of Runes, hoping to uncover the weapon and its secrets. 

The last confirmed report of the armament in Dwarven possession was in the hands of Runesmith Tudnak Haudssen at the time of the last incursion of Chaos into Karak Vlag, when it fell. All traces of the Dwarf hold and those that called it home disappeared, and it was believed that the weapon shared the same fate. 

Many years passed until, just over a century ago, a band of Kislevite trappers operating near the Worlds Edge Mountains encountered a band of Tainted Dwarves. The trappers engaged them in combat, but were massacred to a man. The lone survivor of the trappers, one Ivan Keanovich, escaped to report the encounter and claimed that the leader used an ornate warhammer that could call forth lightning bolts at will. 

An Imperial explorer named Tomas Ostermann came upon a copy of the report and determined that what was essentially a footnote of the retelling was enough to confirm that the weapon used was indeed Gnoldron, and he mounted an expedition to attempt to recover the weapon. His journal, which included an accounting of his investigation and preparation for the expedition, was left with the Temple of Verena in Middenheim. Unfortunately, Tomas was never heard from again. 

Though his reasons for the expedition and what he sought to gain were not amongst his entries, the hammer would easily win its finder a lord’s ransom from any Dwarf King or Rune Lord for its safe return. The chance to find such a treasure has been a cause for no few groups of adventurers making their ways toward Kislev and looking for signs of Tainted Dwarf bands in the mountains to its east. 

## **Grimmaz**
Grimmaz is a Rune Axe, also called “the Harsh Master”. Another weapon crafted during the War of Vengeance, in this case for the Jarlki clan, a ruling clan of Karak Ungor. It is said to have the power to increase the speed and fury of its bearer’s attacks. Additionally, it is also believed that the axe has the ability to destroy an opponent’s weapon regardless of its own enchantments. 

It was used to great effect by Grim Jarlki and gained fame during the storming of the last Elf colony in the Old World at the site of present-day Marienburg. Following the fall of their Dwarf hold Karak Ungor in -1500 IC the Jarlkis, like many other noble clans, found refuge in Karaz-a-Karak. 

Reclamation of the axe has been one of the noted objectives of a number of attempts to retake the hold throughout the years. In –975 IC, King Snorri Morgrimson led the clans to attempt to capture Karak Ungor. This force met with some initial successes, and Strakerd Jarlki, head of the clan at the time, was tasked to hold the southern gate of the Karak while other Dwarven forces worked their way to infiltrate and clear the inhabitants. 

**I** IVI 

An especially aggressive onslaught by Goblins of the Twisted Claw tribe was able to force Strakerd and his warriors from the gate, sealing the fate of those that had moved further in. Ordered by the Dwarf King to hold his position until reinforcements arrived, Strakerd took the loss of his fellow Dwarves as a personal failing and chose to ignore the command. Whether he wanted to redeem himself by reclaiming the gate and purge his shame through heroism, sought personal renown or simply fell foul of his own hubris is not recorded, only that he disobeyed his orders and would ultimately fall while attempting to breach the Goblin lines. 

The contingent was forced back, and eventually retreated to Karaz-a-Karak. 

In the closing stages of the Great War Against Chaos, around 2301 IC, King Belegar led a force of Karak Ungor Dwarves to again attempt to retake the Karak with the intention to use it as a base, as Skalf Dragonslayer had done with nearby Karak Azgal almost a millennia before. Again, the recovery of Grimmaz was considered an immediate objective. Again, the force would be unsuccessful. The occupying greenskins proved too numerous, and in the final skirmish Belegar was mortally wounded. The kingship fell upon his son, Ulfar. The fallen king was returned to Karaz-a-Karak, where he remains interred until the day that Karak Ungor is retaken. 

Given the amount of time that has passed since the weapon was lost, there are a number of conflicting sightings or theories of where the Axe may be. Some claim that the Twisted Goblin tribe who captured it originally passed it to the more dominant Red Eye tribe, before they then traded it to the Hobgoblins east of the Worlds Edge Mountains. Other accounts have stated that it has been seen in the possession of a marauding band of Tainted Dwarfs found near the High ( _Belyevorota_ ) Pass, northeast of Praag. 

Prince Ulther, the most recent leader of the Karak Ungor Dwarfs and grandson of King Belegar, has issued a bounty for any information that may lead to the recovery of the legendary heirloom.
